title: Which Reading Is Right? Errors Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A doctor checks your pulse three times. A tailor measures a sleeve twice. Why measure again and again? Because no measurement is perfect. Diya measures one glass of water five times and gets five different numbers. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn absolute, relative and percentage errors.

You will watch a measuring jug fill five times on a live measuring bench while each reading drops onto a graph with its error bar from the mean. We build the rules step by step: the mean, the absolute error of each reading, the mean absolute error, and the result written as value plus or minus error. Then relative error and percentage error, with side-by-side comparisons (a glass of water vs a spoon of syrup) and two pause-and-think checks. A worked pendulum timing example, the exam trap about signs, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:

0:29 Error and the mean

3:32 Worked example: timing a pendulum
4:08 Exam trap: averaging errors with their signs
4:34 Practice question (NEET pattern)

Next episode: Error Propagation in Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication and Division. A small error in a table's length and width: what is the error in its area?
